page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.3xlarge is a general-purpose, network- and EBS-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, operating at a high clock speed of 5.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI. The instance is equipped with 48.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance, such as stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls into the average (middle 50%) to strong (top 25%) categories. Memory performance is robust, with large-block read and write memory bandwidth testing in the top 25%, though small-block cached reads remain in the middle 50%. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier efficiency in image processing, text processing, and small-model LLM text generation, while maintaining average throughput for database operations and software compilation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8azn.3xlarge offers a high-performance compute profile for workloads that benefit from high single-core clock speeds without requiring massive memory-to-CPU ratios or local NVMe storage. The dedicated core allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. This hardware profile is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, text and image processing pipelines, single-threaded compression tasks, and light-to-medium LLM inference workloads.

It is equipped with 48.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, relying on a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for storage and connectivity. Performance benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU execution, image processing, and text processing, alongside strong large-block memory bandwidth. Multi-core and database operations perform at average to strong levels. This configuration is highly efficient for workloads requiring high single-threaded performance, such as web serving, data compression, and small-scale language model inference, offering a balanced resource profile without the overhead of local storage.
